standard_prerequisites.name: Generation of two-sided subspaces by their constant part
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that a two-sided subspace of the tensor product with a central skew field is generated by its intersection with the constants, which is the substantive input of the argument.

core_obligations: The ideal of constants (proof lines 470-472): the set of elements of the algebra whose tensor with the identity lies in the given two-sided ideal is shown to be a two-sided ideal of the algebra.

The conclusion (proof lines 473-474): the cited lemma on two-sided subspaces generated by their constant part identifies the given ideal with the tensor product of that ideal with the skew field; the final assertion about simplicity follows because the ideal was arbitrary, so a proper nonzero ideal in the tensor product would produce one in the algebra.
proof_roadmap: Cut the given ideal by the constants to get an ideal of the algebra.
Apply the generation lemma to write the ideal as a tensor product.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that every two-sided ideal of the tensor product of an algebra with a central skew field is the tensor product of an ideal of the algebra with the skew field, and consequently that simplicity is preserved by such a tensor product (statement lines 462-468). The proof is a complete argument: the constants lying in the ideal form a two-sided ideal of the algebra, and the cited lemma on two-sided subspaces generated by their constant part identifies the given ideal with the tensor product of that ideal (proof lines 470-474), from which the simplicity statement follows since the ideal was arbitrary. The non-formal content is the reduction to the generation lemma. The claim is H2.
